what_it_does: This paper addresses a serious physical security threat: laser voltage probing attacks, where an attacker shines a laser at the back of a chip to measure electrical voltages and extract secrets. Current defenses are expensive or bulky. The authors propose a sensor-free detection method that watches for telltale signs of these attacks—specifically, tiny changes in how much power the chip leaks when not actively computing—and triggers a shutdown when an attack is detected, all with minimal added chip size (just 4.35% overhead).
